draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Sakleshpur! This hill town on the Hemavati River sits at the foot of the Western Ghats, and trains heading to Mangaluru pick up extra engines here to tackle the steep ghat.
draft.hungryLine: The specialty around here is akki rotti with chicken or pork curry.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Sakleshpur railway station is a 13 min walk, and Manjarabad Fort, shaped like an eight-pointed star, is about 4 km southwest of town.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Head out to the Hemavathi Backwater for a slow, quiet afternoon.
moodReplies.surprise-me: At Sakleshpur station, banker engines are attached to trains heading for Mangaluru so they can climb and descend the ghat's 1:50 gradient safely.

tips.title: Get permission for the Green Route Trek.
tips.body: This famous trek along the railway tracks needs prior permission from the Forest Department.

tips.title: Watch your footing near Yedakumeri.
tips.body: One exit from the trek crosses a shallow river with a rocky, slippery bed.

story.title: A star-shaped fort
story.body: Tipu Sultan built Manjarabad Fort in 1792 with help from French military architects.

story.title: Rails through the ghats
story.body: A metre gauge line ran 147 km from Sakleshpur down to Mangalore, through high bridges and many tunnels.

story.title: A new track
story.body: The Hassan to Mangalore line was converted to broad gauge, funded by a joint venture of the state government and Indian Railways.

story.title: Trekkers' favourite
story.body: The Green Route Trek along the old tracks, from near Donigal to Yedakumeri, draws hikers from Bangalore.
